name: The Backrooms
title: The Yellow Room That Launched a Mythology Was Real
claims: The Backrooms originated in a 2019 thread on 4chan | 1
Thread started May 12, 2019 on /x/, the paranormal board, asking users to post disquieting images that feel "off" | 1
The photo showed an empty room with an uncomfortable yellow atmosphere | 1
Another user named the Backrooms and gave the first description, including the quoted text about noclipping, mono-yellow, fluorescent hum and approximately six hundred million square miles | 1
The photo was taken in 2002 in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, at a former furniture store being renovated by a new tenant | 1
Photo was widely unknown in origin until 2024 | 1
Within days writers shared Backrooms stories on subreddits such as r/creepypasta and r/backrooms | 1
Fans created "levels" and hostile "entities" | 1
Fans who preferred the original split off and created r/TrueBackrooms | 1
ABC News said the lack of a canonical Backrooms made it difficult to draw a line between authentic storytelling and jokes | 1
r/backrooms had over 157,000 members by March 2022 | 1
Fandom spread to YouTube, Twitter, TikTok, Discord, and Fandom and Wikidot wikis that function like the SCP Foundation wiki | 1
Severance creator included the Backrooms among his influences | 1
In May 2024 a Backrooms-dedicated Discord community traced the image to an archived webpage from March 2003 on the Wayback Machine | 1
Building was a former furniture store with plenty of partitions and fake inner walls | 1
Rohner's Home Furnishings occupied the building for much of the 20th century; in 2003 a new tenant, a HobbyTown branch, acquired part of it | 1
Second story renovated in 2002; photographed June 12, 2002 with a Sony Cyber-shot; documented on the renovation blog March 2, 2003 | 1
File name Dsc00161.jpg; carpeted room, yellow wallpaper, fluorescent lighting, Dutch angle | 1
Caption called it the East (Oval) room and noted no windows were visible | 1
Blog entry described extensive water damage that required the area to be cleared | 1
The interior no longer exists; it was converted into a radio-controlled car racing track | 1
By 2024 the building needed renovation and the roof was in disrepair; the owner started a crowdfunding campaign; considered selling wallpaper and carpet samples | 1
Renovation estimated at about $78,000; campaign raised more than $24,000 | 1
In 2025 the building and store were sold; the store continues under a new name | 1
Kotaku said the collaborative aspect and lack of overt horror made the Backrooms stand out from other creepypastas | 1
Kotaku and an internet studies professor said it is scary because it invites you to interpret what is not shown; Kotaku said the horror derives partly from subtle wrongness | 1
Some sources believe the Backrooms was the origin of the liminal spaces aesthetic; #liminalspaces has nearly 100 million TikTok views | 1
Noclip originates in Doom II's idclip command, letting players walk through walls; today it has a broader meaning of glitches where reality's walls come down | 2
Level 0: yellow walls, moist carpet, humming fluorescents; Level 1: concrete, flickering lights, mechanical sounds; Level 2: narrow halls, high heat, few have made it | 2
Many claimed to have entered via dreaming; others described encounters in elevators, construction sites, nursing homes; shared feeling of existential hollowness | 2

January 2022 short film "The Backrooms (Found Footage)" posted on YouTube by Kane Parsons (Kane Pixels), presented as a VHS tape of a filmmaker who enters the Backrooms in the 1990s and is pursued by a monster | 1
Made in a month with Blender and After Effects; Parsons described the Backrooms as a manifestation of a poorly remembered recollection of the late 1990s and early 2000s | 1
Over 90 million views as of August 2026; WPST called it the scariest video on the Internet; Kotaku praised its restraint | 1

Series introduced Async, which opened a portal in the 1980s and conducted research; series disconnected from the internet lore; over 197 million views; credited with lifting the Backrooms into the mainstream | 1
A24 announced a film adaptation on February 6, 2023 with Parsons directing; released in the US on May 29, 2026 | 1
A critic predicted a "slick but dismal 2-hour Hollywood movie" | 1
In May 2026 Parsons said there were things in the works and the web series would continue | 1
An indie game came out two months after the original creepypasta; praised for atmosphere, criticized for short length; many more games followed including Dreamcore in 2025 | 1
An American Horror Stories episode was inspired by the Backrooms | 1
The Poolrooms are a seemingly infinite labyrinth of white-tiled indoor swimming pools, adapted by users as part of the Backrooms; the 2026 film briefly features a scene with them | 1
In 2022 a TikTok trend used Google Earth to reveal supposed Backrooms entrances | 1

sources.title: The Backrooms: An eerie phenomenon lies behind these familiar hallways
